newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka troops advance further into rebel area.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka troops advance further into rebel area.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops on Tuesday advanced further into rebel-held territory, meeting negligible resistance from separatist Tamil guerrillas for the second day, military officials said.

Troops, backed by heavy artillery, tanks and air cover, pushed deeper into the northern Wanni region after advancing about eight km (five miles) on Monday, a military spokesman told Reuters in Colombo.
"Today also they (troops) have advanced and met little resistance," he said.
The spokesman said troops started out from two or three different locations, but declined to say where they were heading.

The Defence Ministry has been tight-lipped on the aim of the latest offensive, which was initially launched on February 4 from Vavuniya, a government stronghold 220 km (138 miles) northeast of Colombo.

The drive resumed on Monday, military officials said, after troops paused for about 10 days to fortify gains following a 22-km (14-mile) push into rebel territory during the first three days of the offensive, code-named "Edi Bala" (Brave Force).
The military spokesman declined to reveal the location of the troops, saying it would pinpoint their whereabouts to Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) fighters.
"We can't give locations now because they (have) artillery. They can hammer our troops," he said.
The rebels shelled Vavuniya 10 days ago, using for the first time long-range artillery they took from a major army camp at northeastern Mullaitivu, which they overran last July.
Two policemen were killed in the artillery attack.
The army has had no casualties in the offensive, the spokesman said.
An LTTE spokesman told Reuters from London that he did not have enough information on the army's advance to comment on it immediately.
"We are watching the developments carefully and will make a statement in the days ahead," he said.
The LTTE are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in this predominantly Sinhalese Indian Ocean island.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE says the toll is much higher.
